differences.what: Overall exposure and white point. Apart from the grade the two frames are the same image: after fitting a tone curve the remaining difference averages 0.7 levels. A never goes above 240 in any channel (its brightest luma is 232), so the white carton bodies sit at 200-227 and look like grey card and the whole frame looks murky. B lifts the same faces to 229-246 without clipping (only 0.05% of pixels reach 248 or above), so the product reads as white.

Blue speaker body and its Nutrition Facts panel. The front white is 203 in A and 230 in B, the side 173 in A and 195 in B. The label paper is whiter in B and its ruled lines are crisper (local contrast 25 against 19), although the label text is unreadable mush in both.
'earmilk' logo on the red base. The white type peaks at about 202 in A, a dull grey on red. In B it peaks at about 230, so it reads as clean white print and the letter edges look crisper.
'earmilk' logo on the blue base: same effect. The type is whiter in B and stands out more against the blue.
Woofer cone highlight. In A the highlight peaks at 206 and is a soft grey streak. In B it peaks at 235 and is a crisp metallic sweep, so the cone looks glossier and more expensive.

Shading on the red tower's front face. B's highlight roll-off squeezes the top of the face into 243-246, so the top-to-bottom shading spans only 17 levels against A's 26 and the upper front panel looks flatter, almost a flat white plane.

Back wall. A's wall is a drab taupe at about 140, which makes the room look underexposed. B's is about 157, lighter and airier, and the product still stands out from it as much as in A (Weber contrast 0.58 against 0.62).
Vase. In A it is grey (median 162). In B it reads as white ceramic (median 184) and its highlights are kept (95th percentile 206, nothing clipped).

Wood on the cabinet doors and floor. B is a little brighter, with more fine contrast (texture measure 3.5 against 2.8 on the doors and 4.5 against 3.5 on the floor), so the wood looks warmer. The procedural contour-line grain with its chevron kinks looks equally artificial in both.
